P1.evidence: The rep referenced the setter handoff but deliberately declined to read it back — 'he just, like, breathed me in, but, like, I'm kind of old-school, and I like to hear it from the person that I'm talking to.' He did later use a note from it ('Kim mentioned to me that you have a pretty packed schedule'), so the prospect was partly made to feel seen. The four-part frame was clean and complete: 'where you are right now, what are you trying to achieve, what have you tried, and how we can actually help you get better and get your results.' Frame agreement was asked and given — 'All right?' / 'Oh, perfect. Thank you so much.' The scripted open question was never asked; the frame simply handed off and the prospect started himself.

P2.evidence: Genuinely good on five of nine. Work was opened first and the desk-bound picture established. Injuries were asked directly, with a smart sector-specific follow-up — 'Any back pains? Because, from the guys that I'm talking to, when they sit a lot, sometimes it results in like lower back pain.' Diet was worked properly, including vegetarian status, chicken frequency and protein source. Energy was asked cleanly. But age was volunteered, not asked, and height and weight were never established at all — the rep later asked for a weight-based goal without ever knowing the starting weight. Sleep was never mentioned. Most seriously, health conditions were never asked: the prospect volunteered 'I have had some health issues, nothing major, but then it's like, you know, you're getting tested and worrying about, like, what's going on' and the rep moved straight past it.

P3.evidence: The bridge to why was run explicitly and well — 'the guys that are getting the best results are the ones that having their deep why behind why they want to do it. So what would be your why?' — and produced real material about independence and not being crippled early. The follow-up 'when you say age gracefully, what does it mean, like, to you specifically?' deepened it further, and the granular version pulled out the shirtless-physique goal. The drive-through to family landed but by assertion rather than question: the rep told him 'we want to stay active for the kids, yeah? You don't want to be that kind of dad that when you're going to be 55, you're going to be sitting on the couch' rather than asking who else it impacts. Nothing physical he currently cannot do was ever surfaced, and the reflect-back — 'so this isn't really about the weight, it's about X, is that right?' — was never delivered, which is the one move that would have locked the why in before price.

P4.evidence: The best-run phase on the call. Past attempts were opened directly — 'You mentioned you tried some apps before' — and the outcome probed. The consistency question was the strongest single move: 'But you also said a very important thing that you didn't stay consistent. Why is that?' The rep also tested for a trigger event and correctly accepted that there wasn't one — 'I thought there was something happening in your life that you realized, okay, enough is enough' / 'no, no, no, nothing... I'm being proactive.' Marked down because the structural gap was named by the prospect unprompted in his opening monologue ('not tailored', 'There is nobody there to correct me') rather than surfaced by the rep, and the 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' line was never delivered.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was not run. The two-year question was never asked, willingness to settle was never tested, and no line in the sand was requested. The rep used the phrase but only inside a description of other clients — 'oftentimes that the guys come here, something like something happened, like a major injury, or they got diabetes' — and when the prospect confirmed no such event had happened, the rep replied 'That's good, that's good' and moved on. That was the moment to build cost of inaction for a preventive buyer, and instead the absence of a crisis was treated as good news. This is the direct cause of the unresolved objection twenty minutes later.

P6.evidence: Belief in the approach was tested repeatedly and answered strongly — 'do you feel like this approach would actually work for you? Because this is the most important thing' / 'Oh, definitely.' The all-in check was run and run well, but in the wrong place: 'Are you fully into this? Like, you want to do this?... Nothing else that would be stopping you?' came after the price, not before it, so the rep bought a clean isolation at the cost of the leverage the script is designed to create. When hesitation surfaced the rep did not return to Phase 5 as instructed; he went to the calendar.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — the investment was presented and the buying question asked — but no attempt was made to collect anything. No card was requested, no link was sent, no deposit was floated even though the manager's stated policy permits one. The onboarding, agreement and welcome-email steps are not applicable because no payment existed to trigger them. The rep proposed a two-day gap, the prospect countered with a week, and the rep accepted immediately: 'Sure. Can we do this like one week from now, if you have time?' / 'Okay. Let's see if we have July.'

objection_plays.detail: 'Let me give it a thought' is a textbook Objection A trigger. The rep ran a good isolation — confirming nothing but money was in the way — but none of the OA moves themselves. He never asked whether the prospect felt this CAN get him to his goal, never asked what makes him feel it can, never asked what is actually preventing him from starting, and never used 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'. The play was substituted with a calendar slot.

Isolation ran cleanly — 'We are talking right now about the logistical part of the equation, the finances' / 'Nothing else that would be stopping you?' The upfront-versus-broken-up move ran in a diluted form: 'most of the guys take it upfront, but if that's your case that you have some other obligations, we can talk about it.' Everything after that was skipped. There was no permission question about having an open, honest conversation about finances, and not one item of the financial picture was collected — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. The single attempt, 'how would it have to look like for you financially, for you to feel comfortable', is too abstract to answer and the prospect duly could not: 'I don't know. I can put a price tag or something on it.'

The timing trigger was explicit and repeated — certifications now, travel in late September, deadlines clearing by the 30th, 'I needed mainly the time.' Not one OD move was run. The rep did not point out that things never slow down, did not name what changes in a week, did not use the compounding argument, and did not offer the 'what if all you had to do was show up' reframe. He conceded the delay and then let it double from two days to seven.

Gap in the script, not a rep failure: the prospect raised a data-security objection about uploading personal training video — 'since I have to send videos and, you know, it's kind of personal, so as long as the platform is secure and that thing is taken care of.' There is no scripted answer. The rep replied 'Absolutely. You're working only with Trevor. There is no other coach over there,' which answers who sees the video, not whether the platform is secure. The prospect accepted it and moved on, so it was never resolved on the merits.

notes: Two very different halves. Discovery through root cause is the best work in this batch — the why question and the consistency question both did real load-bearing work, and the pillar presentation was tailored to what he had actually said. Then the rep skipped the entire consequence frame, ran the commitment check after the price instead of before it, and when the predictable money objection arrived he had no accumulated urgency to draw on and no financial picture to work with. Coach the sequence, not the language: run Phase 5 on preventive buyers especially, because a man with no crisis has no cost of inaction unless you build one for him. Second coaching point: he was on the phone with a fully committed buyer who said the only issue was logistics, and he ended the call with zero dollars and a seven-day gap without floating a deposit, a start date or a single instalment structure.
